How to use this calculator

  1. Enter assessment 1 score, assessment 1 weight, assessment 2 score and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How grade is calculated

Calculate a course average from scores and their percentage weights, then estimate the score needed on a remaining assessment to reach a target. Weights should sum to 100% across completed and remaining work; if they do not, the weighted average is normalized over entered completed work. Scores 85% at 40% weight and 90% at 60% weight yield an 88% course grade. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. Yes; that means the target is mathematically unreachable under the entered weights. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

weighted average = Σ(score × weight) ÷ Σ entered weights
A worked example

Scores 85% at 40% weight and 90% at 60% weight yield an 88% course grade.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Can the required final score exceed 100%?

Yes; that means the target is mathematically unreachable under the entered weights.

Should weights total 100?

They should for a full course plan; the displayed current average normalizes completed weights.
